indicators.note: in tells us the hiss sits inside the word for a ban

parts.note: an interdiction is a ban or prohibition
to hiss at a performer is to boo

explanation.surface: A zoo animal hisses at being told it is not allowed something.
explanation.definitionFit: The baboon is a large African monkey, so it is a primate.

clue.text: Disaster to decorate cake as poisoner?

parts.note: a blow is a setback or disaster
to pipe icing is to decorate a cake

explanation.surface: A baker's catastrophe icing a cake that might be poisoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowpipe fires poisoned darts, so the question mark admits it is a tool of a poisoner.

parts.note: to be is to exist or appear
wilder means more reckless

explanation.surface: Someone seems ever more reckless while in a stupor.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder is to confuse or daze someone.

clue.text: European city in Liverpool soaked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
in shows the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A European city is caught in Liverpool's rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides OLSO across 'Liverpool soaked'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway.

clue.text: Naked energy released by wild streakers

indicators.note: energy released means the letter for energy is let go from the fodder
wild means the remaining letters of streakers run riot into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Streakers running wild at a sports event shed their clothes and their energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'released' takes E out of STREAKERS, and 'wild' rearranges the remaining STRAKERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Starkers is British slang for stark naked, wearing no clothes at all.

clue.text: Patently prolific chap astonished, failing to maintain order

indicators.note: to maintain means the anagram holds the order inside it
failing means the letters break down and are rearranged

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A busy man is astonished when he cannot keep things in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patently' is the joke: Edison was a prolific holder of patents. The anagram letters wrap around the order abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Edison held over a thousand patents, so he was a famously prolific inventor.

indicators.note: in a down clue, topped means the head letter is cut off

parts.note: brush is scrubby wild undergrowth

explanation.surface: Grass grows among the wild undergrowth, its tops cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush is a grass-like marsh plant.

clue.text: The rest almost entirely rewritten for book

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters are set down in a new order
almost entirely means the words lose their final letter

explanation.surface: An editor rewrites nearly all the remainder of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' drops the last T from THE REST, and 'rewritten' rearranges THERES.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a book of the Old Testament.

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are mangled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something unpleasantly damp, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: being sweaty is one way to be unpleasantly damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweaty means damp with perspiration, an unpleasant kind of moisture.

clue.text: Author sick — —-: is that the choice?

definitions.meaning: the writer of Animal Farm and Nineteen Eighty-Four
the blank completes the phrase 'sick ...', a choice between two states of health

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter asks whether a writer is ailing, leaving a blank for the alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap: 'sick ___' becomes 'sick or well', and those two words run together give the writer's pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Blair, the English novelist and essayist.

clue.text: Sweet message written about one group

indicators.note: the message is written around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a note is a short written message
I is the Roman numeral for one
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: A kind note is sent round to a group of friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a hazelnut chocolate, a confection served as a sweet.

clue.text: Changeling having ruffled his feathers, parent initially crushed

indicators.note: ruffled means the letters are disturbed out of order
crushed means all these letters are squashed together and mixed
initially means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A changeling bird ruffles its feathers, its parent crushed beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A changeling in folklore takes another's form, just as a shapeshifter changes its shape.

definitions.meaning: ... position is the front place on a race's starting grid

explanation.surface: A continental driver leads the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Poland is European; in motor racing the leading grid slot is called the pole.

clue.text: By the sound of it, sharp cut

indicators.note: tells us to take a word that is pronounced like the synonym given

parts.note: a sheer or sharp drop is a steep, abrupt one

explanation.surface: A sharp cut, by the sound of it, as a doctor might judge a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: To shear is to clip or cut, as with sheep's wool.

definitions.meaning: a river in Hampshire, England, famous for trout fishing

explanation.surface: An official inspection of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Test is a Hampshire chalk stream; a test is also a trial or check.

clue.text: Tough back on warship, for example

definitions.meaning: the rear part of any vessel, a warship being one example

explanation.surface: A hard man stands at the rear of a naval vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means severe; the stern is also the rear of a boat.

clue.text: Captured by artist, a gentleman's leg

indicators.note: captured by means the letters are held within the following words

explanation.surface: A painter portrays a gentleman's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg' looks like a limb, but it is a stretch of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage is one part of a journey or race, a leg.

parts.note: pretty means fairly or quite, as in pretty good
pretty means attractive or alluring

explanation.surface: A box of chocolates is rather appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean pretty in a twee, sentimental way, like the picture on a chocolate box lid.

indicators.note: protecting means the two words close around the article

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
too means also

explanation.surface: A male bird shields its mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatoo is a crested parrot of Australasia.

parts.note: the word joins two words for a photograph, snap and shot, so it is one picture or two

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves of the word are themselves informal words for a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quickly taken photograph.

definitions.meaning: a carpeting is a severe telling-off
wearing casual rather than smart clothes; threads is slang for clothes

explanation.surface: Floor covering that has been made without fine yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' looks like floor covering, but it is the British sense of a reprimand, as in being called on the carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing-down is a scolding; dressing down is also choosing casual clothes.

parts.note: prim means prudishly proper
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: A respectable American kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: The Primus is a portable paraffin stove used for camping.

clue.text: Literary solver ending in phenomenal scrap

parts.note: Inspector Morse is Colin Dexter's fictional detective, who solves crimes

indicators.note: ending in means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A fictional detective's final scrap is phenomenal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solver' suggests a crossword solver, but it is a detective who solves crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small bite or scrap of food.

definitions.meaning: a black bird of the crow family
a chess piece is called a man; this one is the castle

explanation.definitionFit: A rook is a crow-like bird and also the castle piece in chess.

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing
on means operating or working, as a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: Nothing is working for the American leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Nixon was the 37th president of the United States.

definitions.meaning: to omit something, passing over it

explanation.definitionFit: To skip is both to omit an item and to move with little hops.

definitions.meaning: a sculpture of a head and shoulders

explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a sculpted head and shoulders; bust also means broken.

clue.text: Italian hothead lent an ear, though odd parts ignored

indicators.note: ignoring the odd parts leaves the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered Italian listened, though only to some of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hothead' is a volcano with a fiery summit, not a quick-tempered man.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, a hot-topped Italian mountain.

clue.text: Approaching South American capital, the majority of the majority fly

indicators.note: approaching places the first piece just before the capital
taking the majority of a word means dropping its final letter

parts.note: most means the greater part, the majority
Quito is the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: Near Ecuador's capital, most people have to swat insects.
explanation.definitionFit: The mosquito is a small biting insect, a two-winged fly.

definitions.meaning: to tack is to sew with loose temporary ...; a tack is one such
a sharp pain in the side after running

explanation.surface: A drawing pin that hurts a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A tack is a loose sewing stitch; a stitch is also a mild side pain.

clue.text: One in capital of Spain or Italy, lost!

indicators.note: capital here means the first letter of the word
lost means the letters are mixed up and astray

explanation.surface: A tourist in Madrid or Rome is lost and alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary is a hermit or recluse, one who lives alone.

indicators.note: the solver is placed in the temple

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
the clue addresses the solver as you

explanation.surface: The solver is told something odd while visiting a temple.
explanation.definitionFit: Way-out is informal for strange or unconventional.
